content:
zoe: New hire trying the macOS quickstart (M1) — followed README, installed brew package, exported REDWOOD_KEY, but first chat POST returns 402. UI shows trial active. Anybody seen key/cache weirdness on mac?

raj: Was the key set in terminal or stored in Keychain? The mac installer has a helper that optionally saves the token to Keychain and the sample CLI will prefer keychain over env.

zoe: I put it in env (export REDWOOD_KEY=xxx) and also clicked 'save to keychain' in the installer. Sample app prints "using key from keychain" in logs (masked).

clare: Repro often: user thinks env is used but CLI picks keychain. If the keychain entry is from a previous demo org (stale), the UI can still show trial for the new org but API uses stale key -> 402.

zoe: Confirmed: `security find-generic-password -s redwood` shows old token. Host curl with env works, but quickstart binary (which queries Keychain) sends the old one.

zoe: ```
# host (works)
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
# container/binary (fails)
# Authorization: Bearer <masked-old-token> -> 402 Payment Required
```

raj: Two separate DX bugs colliding: (A) starter prefers keychain/file over env without explicit logging, (B) SDK+starter default retry policy retries on 402, so users see repeated 402s which is confusing.

clare: Also saw an auth-parity note: older SDK versions used `Authorization: Token <key>` header. Gateway tolerated that for active workspaces but returned erratic 401/402 during provisioning. Which SDK version is the quickstart using?

zoe: Quickstart uses CLI v0.2.1 which bundles SDK 0.9.x. I ran `./quickstart --print-key-source` and it said keychain.

devops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-202 mac-keychain-credential-cache-and-retry-loop  https://go.redwood.ai/inc/INC-2026-202

raj: Short-term fixes: (1) quickstart: prefer env var if present and log the chosen source clearly (env|keychain|file) with masked value; (2) change starter to print a clear hint when it sees 402: "Workspace looks like it's still provisioning. Visit: https://app.redwood.ai/workspaces/<id>/billing or wait 30s and retry"; (3) SDK: do not retry on 402 billing_required.

clare: I'll add a tiny guard in the quickstart that does GET /v1/workspaces/me and checks state=="active" before making the first interactive request. If not active, show a spinner + message and poll up to 60s.

zoe: That would be great. Right now my logs show three failed POSTs, each with slightly different stack traces. The retries made debugging painful.

sdk-lint: Filed SDK ticket SDK-530: "Treat 402 billing_required as terminal; add wait_for_workspace_ready helper". Also adding a lint rule to quickstart templates to prefer a preflight check.

starter-bot: Issue opened: redwood-inference/starter#923 "mac: prefer REDWOOD_KEY env over Keychain + verbose source log, add preflight workspace check"

raj: Long-term: unify credential precedence across SDKs (env > keychain > file) and make the default quickstart surface obvious logging. Also consider a CLI flag `--no-keychain` to opt out.

zoe: Implemented a quick local hack: removed the stale key from Keychain and re-ran. After ~18s provisioning flipped and first POST succeeded. Will open a PR for the quickstart change.

clare: Thanks. If you can include repro steps for the stale-key keychain scenario that helps ops reproduce. Closing once PR merged. :raised_hands:
